text: The Go menu shows ⌘[, ⌘] and ⌘↑, and File › Move to Trash shows ⌘⌫. The Back button's tooltip shows ⌘[, and one press of ⌘[ goes back one folder.
The menu bar shows ⌘R for View › Refresh, ⌘O for File › Open and ⌘Y for File › Quick Look. They used to show F5, Return and Space.
A two-finger click on Back opens a menu of the places it leads to. Its tooltip reads Back to “name” with ⌘[. Resizing the window while the menu is open closes it.
Search, open a folder from the results, then press ⌘[ twice and ⌘] twice. Back should return to the results, then to the folder you searched from.
In a new window Back and Forward are dimmed, in light and dark. With a system accent colour other than blue, the other toolbar buttons look as they did.
⌘Return on one selected search result opens its folder with the item selected. The item menu shows ⌘↩ beside Show in Enclosing Folder.
⌘S during a search opens Save Smart Folder; outside a search it shows a short notice. Edit › Save Search… does the same. With --term, try Ctrl+S: some terminals keep it for flow control.
In Settings at 110% text size, the controls at the bottom of the dialog can still be reached. Settings › Nushell › Choose… keeps a symlinked nu as the path you picked.
A zip file's preview scrolls to its last row with the trackpad and bounces at its ends like the other previews. A wide table still scrolls sideways.
Opening a contents-search result shows the preview at the matching line, highlighted. Watch for an empty frame before the text appears.
With Quick Look's window open beside the browser, Return in the search field moves into the results, and Quick Look still answers Escape, Space and the arrow keys.

Window › Show Next Tab and Show Previous Tab: check whether the menu shows ⌃T and ⌃⇧T, and whether Ctrl+T switches tabs. This is older code that was only read, not changed: GPUI's menu code has no symbol for the Tab key.
Search one folder for a name that isn't there with Kind set to Image: “No Results” names the folder and the kind, both buttons work, and the Kind button is tinted in your accent colour.

Drag the window by the empty part of the toolbar, then press an arrow key: the selection in the files still moves. With the sidebar as a folder tree, click a tree row, hide the sidebar with ⌥⌘S, and press ⌥⌘S again: it comes back.
A two-finger swipe over the tabs scrolls them, sideways and up or down. With six or more tabs, ⌘\ keeps the showing tab in view. Right-click a tab, then drag the window's edge: the menu closes.

Double-click Done in Settings while a file is under the pointer: the file does not open. Then double-click a file: it opens as before. Close Quick Look's window with a click and click a file right away: it is selected.
Open a folder of photos, HEIC included, in the icon view and the gallery: tiles show the kind icon and then a thumbnail, and memory stays flat while you scroll.
Drag files from Finder onto another tab: they are copied into its folder. Option-drag an item from fffinder onto a tab: it is copied, not moved. A mouse's middle button closes a tab.
Right after launch, go to Recents while the index is still being built: placeholders show, not the last folder's files. Step between folders on the local disk: no flash in between.

A Smart Folder's filter, kind and scope now end with its search, so the next folder you open is no longer filtered. If you used a Smart Folder to load a filter and then browse, type the filter in the filter bar instead.
Save for Smart Folders moved from the Nushell filter bar to the scope bar of every search, and ⌘S saves the current search.
Back during a search only ends the search and stays in its folder. It used to go on to the previous place as well. Back and Forward now return to earlier searches.
Escape in an empty search field gives the keyboard back to the files. In a --pick chooser, pressing Escape repeatedly in the search field now ends in Cancel.
Equally good matches are listed newest first, then by path, across all search locations. They used to come one search location after another.
Name searches and Recents update by themselves a few seconds after another program adds, removes or renames a file. Contents searches still wait for Refresh (⌘R).

Kind: Document matches every type the Kind column calls a document, including .log, .conf, .env, .ini and .plist. With your home folder as a search location, ~/Library's .plist and .log files match a Document search. Taking a type out is an edit of one list in crates/fffinder-core/src/kind.rs.
A capital letter in a search word no longer forces an exact-case match: README finds readme.md. Capitals now only raise the rank of names that fit them.
Search results start at the top with nothing selected whenever the words, scope or kind change. Ending a search puts the folder back as it was, selection and scroll position included.
A folder filter such as `notes/ todo` keeps to folders named exactly notes, whatever the kind. It used to match meeting-notes/ as well.
Sorting search results chooses among every match, up to 20,000 per search location, so a click on a column can run the search again. It used to reorder only the items already listed.
In the column view, the wheel over a long table preview scrolls the table. It used to move the columns sideways.
New key: ⌘Return (Ctrl+Enter on Linux and Windows) shows the selected result in its enclosing folder.
New option: `--here` searches only the folder a command opens, as in `fffinder ~/src --query readme --here`. `fff gui`, `fff pick` and the other Nushell commands take it too.

An empty file area says why it is empty. A filter that hides everything reads “No Items Pass the Filter” with a Remove Filter button, and “No Results” names the folder and kind the search was limited to, with Search This Computer and Search Any Kind buttons.

With Allow typos on, a search that matches nothing exactly lists only near misses: one typo in a word of four to seven letters, two from eight letters, none in a word of three or fewer. Some loose searches that used to find their file now find nothing, such as `prjatlz` for Project Atlas.txt.

A click on a row of the sidebar's list, the path bar, the status bar or the empty part of a bar no longer takes the keyboard away. The arrow keys and typing go on working in the files, or in the search field if it had the keyboard.
With more tabs than fit, the tab bar scrolls sideways with the wheel or a swipe, and + stays at the end. A tab you open or switch to scrolls into view.
Collapsing every group keeps the group headers on screen; it used to say the folder was empty. An empty folder now has the right-click menu with New Folder and Paste.

A preview is read again when its file changes: a couple of seconds after another program saves it, the Preview Pane, the gallery and Quick Look show the new contents. Refresh and switching between light and dark no longer leave a preview on a spinner.

An item opens only when both clicks of a double-click are on it. A double-click on a dialog's Done or Cancel no longer opens the file under the pointer, and clicking on quickly after opening a folder no longer opens folder after folder.

In the column view an item stays selected when its column is read again, sorted or refreshed; it used to jump to a neighbour. Sort By now sorts every column, and Escape clears the selection there as in the other views.
New Folder opens its group when the group is collapsed, and under a Nushell filter the new folder stays listed while you name it. The status bar now counts the items of collapsed groups.

Image tiles show a thumbnail fffinder makes itself instead of loading every photo whole, so a folder of photos no longer fills memory. An image saved again shows its new picture once its folder is read again.
Tabs take more from the mouse: drop items on another tab to move or copy them into its folder, middle-click a tab to close it, and a tab's right-click menu has Close Other Tabs.

After you go to another place, the previous place's items can no longer be selected, opened or dragged. They show for a sixth of a second at most, then placeholders take their place until the new place has been read.
A search word with a capital runs two searches, so that capitals can count as a preference instead of a requirement. A simpler one-search version was written and set aside.
Disabled toolbar buttons use the UI kit's standard dimming, which is fainter than disabled menu items. A one-line change at three call sites gives the stronger look.
The highlighted matching line is drawn in the plain text colour and loses its syntax colours, so that it reads on the highlight.
A table preview's heading row scrolls away with the first rows. Keeping it in view needs a hand-built scroll area, as explore mode has.
The Mac's menu bar has no File › Show in Enclosing Folder. GPUI has no menu symbol for Return, so the item would most likely show, and might act on, ⌘E.
Settings accepts any file as nu without running it first. A wrong pick shows an error naming the file wherever Nushell is used, and Find Automatically undoes it.
A one-letter search of a search location with more than 20,000 files now lists folders too, at the cost of as many of its older files.
Rename… and Update with Current Search for a Smart Folder were left out. Saving under the same name replaces it in place and says so.
Live results are paced. A rerun waits for files to stop coming, half a minute at most, and backs off to about once in four minutes while reruns change nothing.
The buttons under “No Results” are for the mouse only. Tab skips them, because Return and Space in the file area mean Open and Quick Look.
The title stays “No Results” without the words searched for. The message stays up while a search runs again, so it would name words that have no answer yet.

A single letter or digit typed beside a longer word no longer narrows a search; it only ranks. `photo 2` lists every photo with photo 2.jpg first. Making digits narrow again is one condition in `checked_words` in the engine.
The tab bar comes back to the showing tab whenever its width changes, also after you scrolled away from it by hand. One listener at the end of `render_tab_bar` decides this.

A stray second click does nothing at all; it does not select the file under it. A sloppy double-click that starts just beside an item no longer opens it, and the column view is the least forgiving about that.

A folder named under a filter it doesn't pass leaves the list when you press Return, with nothing saying it was made; the filter bar and the status bar's count are what explain it. The group that opened for a new folder stays open.

Small copies of the photos you browse are now kept on disk, in thumbnails/ in fffinder's data folder (capped at 256 MB), also for photos on volumes since removed. PDF and video thumbnails were already kept there.
Large image previews keep only the last three per tab or pane. Going back to an older one decodes it again, with its place empty meanwhile.
Cargo.toml turns on seven image formats of the `image` crate the project already uses (no new crate; GPUI builds them anyway).
A middle click closes a tab without asking, and a closed tab can't be reopened. Quick middle clicks at one spot close one tab after another. `close_tab_at_press` is the one place to change that.
The old items stay on screen for 150 ms (`LEFT_BEHIND_STAY` in src/finder/mod.rs). A folder that takes a little longer than that to read, as on a network volume, flashes placeholders on every step.
A search can still vary from run to run where one search location has more than 2,000 further matches that score exactly like the last one kept.
A new typo match is not noticed until Refresh. Large folders outside every search location are not live until the next keystroke or Refresh.
On Windows, a search word typed with a forward slash (src/main) never counts as an exact match, because Windows paths use backslashes. This could not be run here.
`fffinder FILE --query words` does not select the file in its folder when the search ends.
The Nushell panel's field has no Escape of its own. A selection lost when a filter hides its item does not come back when the filter is emptied.
A context menu whose button moves or disappears keeps the keyboard until the next click, for example the item menu after switching views with ⌘2.
With nu 0.116 a MessagePack file previews as a one-column table of bytes, though the manual lists it among the files shown as tables, and an .xlsx shows one row per sheet.
`fff pick` treats every failure other than exit status 2 as a cancelled chooser. On Linux with no display, `fffinder --pick` neither fails nor exits.
Move Tab to New Window carries a search's words only. Its scope, Name or Contents, kind and filter are lost.
A hidden file shown in its enclosing folder while hidden files are off opens the folder with nothing selected.
Look Again gives no sign when it still finds no nu.
In a large folder a misspelled word usually has accidental matches, so the file you meant is still dropped and the accidental ones are listed. A follow-up for this is queued.
A name that stores an accent apart from its letter, as macOS writes names, is found only loosely by typing the letter, and not at all with Allow typos off. A follow-up for this is queued.
A shortcut that leaves the folder while a name is being edited, such as Back or Enclosing Folder, drops what was typed. The keyboard is rescued; the name is not.
A right-click or middle-click on a toolbar button gives that button the keyboard, so Return and Space then press it. The UI kit does this.
Nothing shows that more tabs exist beyond the bar's edge, and a tab can't be dragged onto one that is out of view.
A file written over in place, which changes nothing about its folder, shows as it was until Refresh; an image written over with its date kept is not read again even then.
Loads for items you have already moved past are still not cancelled: holding an arrow key starts one preview load per item passed. That half of the plan was left out.
In the column view, Paste, New Folder and New File always go to the window's folder, even when a later column is the one in use. The status bar's selection count does not follow the column in use.

HEIC and RAW photos are shown large from the system's own thumbnail, which is still kept for the session, so the gallery over iPhone originals still grows by about 3 MB per photo shown. Tile thumbnails are not freed during a session either.
Holding a drag over a tab does not switch to that tab, as Finder does. Close Other Tabs has no key and is not in the menu bar.
README.md and docs/manual.md say Rust 1.92 or newer. For macOS the GPUI dependency (gpui-pre-macos 0.3.10) did not compile with Rust 1.97.0 here; the cross-checks use 1.100.0. Not changed.
GitHub Actions is not enabled on the fork, so the repository's own CI has not run on this branch. Enabling it would run the real macOS and Windows jobs on every push, with no pull request needed.

A triple click on Search This Computer now presses Search Any Kind with its third click when that button has come under the pointer, and Search Any Kind saves Any as the kind. Before, clicks after a double-click did nothing until the mouse rested or moved. If the next button should wait for a pause, one guard decides it.

Search Only in a folder typed in another letter case has never run: Linux tells the cases apart, so its test returns early there. On a Mac, with your home folder as a search location, `fffinder ~/documents --query <a word in a name there> --here` should list matches where it said No Results. Also worth one try: a folder on an exFAT, FAT or network volume, opened the normal way, should still be searchable.

A folder reached through a symbolic link is now searched where the link points, and its results show that place, not the link (unless Follow symbolic links is on). A link or a `..` that leads outside the search locations builds a temporary index of the folder it leads to, which can be a whole volume.

Windows, read and not run: when a link or a `..` leads outside the search locations, the folder is searched by the path Windows resolves it to, which begins with `\\?\`. Results there would show that prefix in their paths, and opening one from the list may fail. Before this change such a folder found nothing at all.

With a Nushell filter on, opening a folder that holds folders now runs `nu` twice (again once the folder sizes are in), and a folder whose files are saved again and again runs the filter at each reread, at most every two seconds. Refresh always runs the filter again.

A file saved the usual quick way (written in place) still does not make a name search or Recents read again, so its row keeps the old size and date until the list is next made. What is fixed is the fresh answer that was read and then thrown away.

A folder renamed in the sidebar's tree and confirmed with Return no longer takes the selection among the files when other items are selected there. It follows from the rule that fixes the wrong-file menu: a right-click on a file that is already selected looks the same as Return. With nothing else selected the folder is selected under its new name, as before.

Two cases remain. A click on an item inside the folder whose name is being edited still ends with the folder selected, so Cmd+Backspace right after it moves the folder to the Trash (the highlight shows the folder). And search results inside a folder renamed in the window keep their old paths until the search runs again; their commands fail with a notification.

Accented names were not run on a Mac. That Finder stores `é` as the letter followed by its accent, and that typed text arrives as one character, are from knowledge. To try: make `Résumé.pdf` in Finder, then search `résumé` and `resume`. Both should list it with the word highlighted, also with Allow typos off.

A word typed without accents now finds names that have them, listed after the names with the word as typed: `resume` finds `Résumé.pdf`, `cafe` finds `Café.app`, and a one-letter search `e` also lists names that only have `é`. A word typed with an accent is taken as typed, so `résumé` does not find `resume.pdf`.

The engine crate now depends directly on `icu_normalizer`. The UI kit already builds that crate, so Cargo.lock gains no new package, only the link. The write-up left a new dependency to you; if you would rather not have it in the engine, that is the line to take out, and the feature with it.

For names that store each accent in one character with its letter (names made on Windows or Linux), a word typed without accents finds them only up to two accented letters per word, ranks them among the loose matches, and in a large folder can leave them out. Names stored the macOS way are found fully.

Cost where most names are not plain ASCII (a Korean, Japanese or Chinese home folder): a search took 3.5 times as long in a debug build on a 30,000-file test tree. Not measured in a release build. On an ASCII tree the difference is between nothing and 6%.

With Allow typos on, near misses of a word are now listed whenever no result has the word as typed, beside the results that have its letters in order. So a misspelled word finds its file in a large folder (`benchmrak` finds `benchmark.rs`), and a search by letters with gaps, such as `pckg`, can list a near miss such as `pkg-config` beside or ahead of `package.json`. With Allow typos off nothing changes.

A name ranks 30 points higher when one of its words begins with a near miss of a word of five letters or more. The reviewer chose five where the implementer had six: five puts more misspelled names first (33 of 41 against 17 in the test tree), and costs searches that type five letters across a folder and a name (`libbu` for a `build.rs` under a folder beginning with lib went from first to tenth). It is one constant, `NEAR_NAME_LETTERS`.

Four-letter words get their near misses listed but not ranked, so `mian` lists a folder named Many ahead of `main.rs`. Apps are still found by letters in order only (`safair` finds no Safari). A new file that is only a near miss of the search waits for Refresh.
